messages.author: 912329a6ad1a6995
messages.subject: Re: some features I miss
parts:
Although it may give Hadley and Winston indigestion :), you can hack your way to a horizontal bar chart.

I imagine there are better ways to do this, but here's one.

Ian

library(dplyr)
library(ggvis)

cocaine %>%
  mutate(month = as.factor(month)) %>%
  ggvis(x = ~month) %>%
  layer_bars() 

cocaine %>%
  mutate(month = as.factor(month)) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarize(count = n()) %>%
  ggvis(x = ~month, width = band(), y = ~count, y2 = 0) %>%
  layer_rects() %>%
  scale_numeric("y", expand = 0)

cocaine %>%
  mutate(month = as.factor(month)) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarize(count = n()) %>%
  ggvis(x = ~count, x2 = 0, y = ~month, height = band()) %>%
  layer_rects() %>%
  scale_numeric("x", expand = 0)

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: some features I miss
parts:
Regarding 3, horizontal bar graphs are possible with layer_rects, but it requires being a bit more explicit. This is similar to Ian's code:

# Continuous y values
pressure %>% ggvis(y = ~temperature -10 , x = ~pressure) %>%
  layer_rects(x2 = 0, y2 = ~temperature+10)

# Categorical y values
pressure %>% ggvis(y = ~factor(temperature), x = ~pressure) %>%
  layer_rects(x2 = 0, height = band()) %>%
  scale_nominal("y", reverse = TRUE, padding = 0.2)
